metadata.note: The Penn Central Transportation Company, 1968-1976 -- the largest railroad merger in American history and, at its 1970 collapse, the largest corporate bankruptcy the United States had yet seen. Penn Central is given its own features here, in its own colour (Penn Central black, the company's actual locomotive livery), rather than being buried as segment notes inside its predecessors, so that dragging the slider to any year from 1968 to 1976 shows the system as one railroad instead of a dozen differently-coloured predecessor companies. Each feature reuses the geometry of the predecessor corridor it came from, named in 'predecessor_feature'; the predecessor's own feature now ends where Penn Central begins, and the modern operator's feature (SEPTA, Metro-North, NJ Transit, MBTA) resumes at Conrail in 1976. Corporate chronology: the Pennsylvania Railroad's acquisition of the New York Central concluded February 1 1968; the New York, New Haven and Hartford was merged in on December 31 1968 at the insistence of the Interstate Commerce Commission; the board voted to file for bankruptcy June 21 1970; Amtrak took over intercity passenger service May 1 1971; and Penn Central's viable rail operations were transferred to Conrail on April 1 1976. That is why ex-PRR and ex-NYC corridors here start in 1968 while ex-New Haven ones start in 1969. NOT included, because they were never merged into Penn Central: the Pittsburgh and Lake Erie Railroad, which stayed a separate corporation and became independent again in 1976, and the jointly PRR/Reading-owned Pennsylvania-Reading Seashore Lines. The Southern Crescent is also excluded -- Southern Railway ran that train over Penn Central rails, but the service was Southern's. || 2026-08-24: resynced pc-michigan-central-lansing-saginaw to its predecessor's corrected geometry, which had been re-traced onto the correct JL&S alignment.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penn_Central_Transportation_Company ("The legal merger (formally, an acquisition of the NYC by the PRR) concluded on February 1, 1968"; "On June 21, 1970 ... the board of directors voted to file for bankruptcy protection under Section 77 of the Bankruptcy Act"; "On April 1, 1976, PC's viable rail operations were transferred to the federally owned Consolidated Rail Corporation (Conrail)")
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York,_New_Haven_and_Hartford_Railroad ("At the insistence of the Interstate Commerce Commission, the New Haven was merged into Penn Central on December 31, 1968")

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_and_Lake_Erie_Railroad ("The P&LE operated as an independent subsidiary, even after New York Central and Pennsylvania Railroad merged to form Penn Central"; became independent again when Conrail was formed) -- basis for excluding the P&LE from this file
Route geometry and speed values are inherited unchanged from the predecessor features named in each feature's 'predecessor_feature' property; see those files for their own geometry sourcing.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Every headway in this file is inherited from the predecessor feature's Penn Central-era segment and is an estimate -- no Penn Central timetable or Official Guide listing has been consulted for any corridor, and the single flat headway per feature hides the fact that service was collapsing throughout the period. Segment boundaries are corporate dates, not service dates: a corridor shown ending in 1971 ends because Amtrak took over intercity service on May 1 1971, not because a documented last train ran. Freight-only years are not distinguished from years with passenger service. The Saginaw Division feature is included on the basis that Penn Central operated the ex-Michigan Central line from 1968, but the source file's own notes never asserted a Penn Central era for it, and whether it still carried passengers that late is unverified. Geometry is the modern/predecessor alignment throughout and does not reflect any Penn Central-era realignment or abandonment.
metadata.chicago_terminal_note: Chicago end truncated Aug 2026. The trace previously ran past its terminal, doubled back south down the ex-Illinois Central main line to 71st Street, then jumped 9 km further south and 18 km back north to a downtown-Chicago anchor point that lay on no track at all. It now ends where the route reaches the ex-Illinois Central main at 18th Street -- the approach to Central Station, the Michigan Central's Chicago passenger terminal from 1893. Note the Chicago approach still contains straight-line chords of about 7.8 km and 5.0 km where the trace is incomplete, and follows the modern NS Chicago Line alignment rather than the historic Michigan Central/Illinois Central route in from Kensington.
metadata.freight_only_audit: 2026-08-24: removed feature 'pc-prr-northern-central-sodus-elmira' (Penn Central: Sodus Bay Branch, Sodus Point - Elmira, 1968-1976). It was added earlier the same day as a deliberate freight-only feature -- passenger service over that branch ended with the last mixed train on November 15 1935 and the last coal boat loaded at Sodus Point on December 11 1967 -- which is exactly what CLAUDE.md Rule 1 forbids. The predecessor feature pennsylvania_railroad_system.geojson#prr-northern-central-sodus-elmira remains and correctly ends in 1936. This also removed the only use of a non-standard mode value, 'freight_rail'.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
